title: Per-IdP configuration specifics: SAML and SCIM for Entra ID, Okta, Ping and Google Workspace; SAML only for AD FS, OneLogin and CA SSO

prose.text: The IdP object itself (fields, default IdP, criteria) is in [[zia.authentication.identity-providers]]; this subject holds what each vendor's configuration guide says differently.

prose.label: Hosts to exempt from authentication.
prose.text: {{entra-exempt-hosts}} {{other-exempt-hosts}} The exemption lists themselves are in [[zia.authentication.exemptions]].

prose.label: Older IdPs.
prose.text: {{adfs-3-claims}} {{adfs-2-claims}} {{casso-quirks}} Whether SCIM works with the SAML-only guides is open {{gap:saml-only-guides-scim}}.

checks.do: Which IdP vendor the tenant uses and whether it supports signed SAML requests, before enabling Sign SAML Request.
Whether the IdP's login hosts are in the Exempted URLs list, and in the PAC file's exemption list when PAC files are used.
Whether the SAML attribute names the IdP sends match the Login Name, User Display Name, Group Name and Department Name attributes configured on the Zscaler IdP, which are case-sensitive.

okta-features.statement: The Okta guide lists Just-in-Time (JIT) Provisioning (SAML auto-provisioning) among the supported SAML features, and the SCIM features supported by the Zscaler and Okta integration as Create Users, Update User Attributes, Deactivate Users and Group Push. Deactivate Users means a user deleted or deactivated in Okta, or with Internet & SaaS unassigned, is also deactivated in the Zscaler service.

quotes: - Just-in-Time (JIT) Provisioning (SAML auto-provisioning)
The SCIM features supported by the Zscaler and Okta integration are:
Deactivate Users: If a user account is deleted or deactivated in Okta or has Internet & SaaS unassigned, the user is also deactivated in the Zscaler service.

evidence.after: The SCIM features supported by the Zscaler and Okta integration are:
quotes: - Create Users
- Update User Attributes
- Deactivate Users
- Group Push

pingone-features.statement: The PingOne guide lists the SCIM features supported by the Zscaler and PingOne integration as Create Users, Update User Attributes, Delete Users and Group Push.

quotes: The following SCIM features are supported by the Zscaler and PingOne integration:
- Create Users
- Update User Attributes
- Delete Users
- Group Push

google-features.statement: The Google Workspace guide lists Deactivate Users among its supported SCIM features, and says Google Workspace does not support Sign SAML Request, On-Demand Provisioning for Users or Group Push. On the Deprovisioning page the administrator specifies an action and time for when an app is turned off for a user, a user is suspended from Google, and a user is deleted from Google.

quotes: The SCIM features supported by the Zscaler and Google Workspace integration are:
- Deactivate Users
Google Workspace does not support the following features:
7. On the Deprovisioning page, specify an action and time for:
- When an app is turned off for a user
- When a user is suspended from Google
- When a user is deleted from Google

evidence.after: Google Workspace does not support the following features:
quotes: - Sign SAML Request
- On-Demand Provisioning for Users
- Group Push

sp-initiated-gateway.statement: In the Okta, PingOne and Google Workspace guides' SP-initiated SSO flow, the user is redirected to https://gateway.<Zscaler cloud Name>.net and prompted for a username.

quotes: 2. You are redirected to https://gateway.<Zscaler cloud Name>.net and prompted for a username.
- You are redirected to https://gateway.<Zscaler cloud Name>.net and prompted for a username.
2. You are redirected to https://gateway.<Zscaler Cloud Name>.net and prompted for a username.

okta-prerequisites.statement: For Okta, a SCIM provisioning subscription for Okta is needed (the guide says to contact the Okta representative). In the Okta app, the Your Zscaler Domain field takes the cloud name (for example zscalerbeta.net), and the guide says a wrong value prevents authenticating via SAML to Zscaler.

quotes: A SCIM provisioning subscription for Okta. Contact your Okta representative to ensure your organization has the appropriate subscription.
Your Zscaler Domain: Enter your cloud name (e.g., zscalerbeta.net).
Make sure to enter the correct value. Using the wrong value prevents you from authenticating via SAML to Zscaler.

ping-prerequisites.statement: The PingFederate and PingOne guides each list a server with the Zscaler Connector add-on as a prerequisite. The PingFederate guide defers SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning configuration to the PingFederate documentation.

quotes: PingFederate server with the Zscaler Connector add-on
To configure SAML Single Sign-On (SSO) and SCIM Provisioning with Zscaler and PingFederate, refer to the PingFederate documentation.
PingOne server with the Zscaler Connector add-on

entra-prerequisites.statement: For Microsoft Entra ID, a premium subscription is highly recommended to avoid restricted functionality, and groups must be assigned to the enterprise application for Entra ID to send group memberships to Zscaler. The guide recommends the provisioning scope Sync only assigned users and groups, lists an optional setting under which deleting groups and users over a threshold requires admin approval, and says that for Seamless SSO the domain hint ?whr=<your organization's domain> must be appended to the Login URL.

quotes: Although you can set some configurations with a free Microsoft Entra subscription, a premium subscription is highly recommended to avoid restricted functionality.
To ensure that Microsoft Entra ID sends group memberships to Zscaler, you must assign groups to the enterprise application.
Scope: (Optional) Select Sync only assigned users and groups. Zscaler recommends enabling this setting.
When the option is enabled, deleting a number of groups and users over the threshold requires approval from an admin.
(Optional) for Seamless SSO, you must append the domain hint ?whr=<your organization's domain> to the end of the Login URL.

okta-no-signing.statement: The Okta guide says Sign SAML Request must be disabled in the Zscaler Admin Console, because Okta doesn't support signed SAML responses from the service provider.

quotes: Ensure the Sign SAML Request option is disabled in the Zscaler Admin Console. Okta doesn't support signed SAML responses from the service provider.

entra-pingone-signing.statement: The Entra ID and PingOne guides both say Zscaler recommends the SHA-2 (256-bit) signature algorithm. In Entra ID, Require verification certificates is enabled, and Allow requests signed with RSA-SHA1 is enabled if SHA-1 (160-bit) was selected in the Admin Console; in PingOne, Enforce Signed AuthRequest is enabled.

quotes: Signature Algorithm: Zscaler recommends selecting SHA-2 (256-bit).
Require verification certificates: Enable this option.
Allow requests signed with RSA-SHA1: If you selected SHA-1 (160-bit) in the Zscaler Admin Console, enable this option.
Signature Algorithm: Zscaler recommends selecting SHA-2 (256-bit).
6. Enable Enforce Signed AuthRequest.

entra-saml-attributes.statement: In the Entra ID guide the Zscaler IdP's Login Name Attribute is NameID, User Display Name Attribute displayName, Group Name Attribute groups and Department Name Attribute Department, each case-sensitive. The claim steps select the source attribute Cloud-only group display names in one step and sAMAccountName in another for groups, and user.department for the department.

quotes: Login Name Attribute: Enter NameID (case sensitive).
User Display Name Attribute: Enter displayName (case sensitive).
Group Name Attribute: Enter groups (case sensitive).
Department Name Attribute: Enter Department (case sensitive).
For Source attribute, select Cloud-only group display names.
For Source attribute, select sAMAccountName.
Source attribute: Enter user.department (case sensitive).

okta-saml-attributes.statement: In the Okta guide the User Display Name Attribute is DisplayName, the Group Name Attribute memberOf and the Department Name Attribute Department, each case-sensitive. Zscaler recommends the memberOf condition be a regular expression .*, so all groups the user belongs to are sent in the SAML assertion.

quotes: User Display Name Attribute: Enter DisplayName (case sensitive).
Group Name Attribute: Enter memberOf (case sensitive).
Department Name Attribute: Enter Department (case sensitive).
Zscaler recommends to set the condition to a regular expression (Regex) with the expression being .*. This means that all groups the user belongs to are sent in the SAML assertion.

pingone-saml-attributes.statement: In the PingOne guide the User Display Name Attribute is displayName, the Group Name Attribute memberOf and the Department Name Attribute department, each case-sensitive.

quotes: User Display Name Attribute: Enter displayName (case-sensitive).
Group Name Attribute: Enter memberOf (case-sensitive).
Department Name Attribute: Enter department (case-sensitive).

google-saml-attributes.statement: In the Google Workspace guide the User Display Name Attribute is DisplayName and the Department Name Attribute is Department (case-sensitive), the Group Name Attribute is optional and can be left blank, and the Name ID format is EMAIL with Name ID from Basic Information > Primary email.

quotes: User Display Name Attribute: Enter DisplayName (case-sensitive).
Group Name Attribute: (Optional) Specify a group name attribute or leave this field blank.
Department Name Attribute: Enter Department (case-sensitive).
Name ID format: In the drop-down menu, select EMAIL.
Name ID: In the drop-down menu, select Basic Information > Primary email.

onelogin-nameid.statement: In the OneLogin guide, the default values select Email for the NameID (Login).

quotes: Default values: Select Email for the NameID (Login).

entra-exempt-hosts.statement: The Entra ID guide has login.windows.net, login.microsoftonline.com, .windowsazure.com, aadcdn.msauth.net and aadcdn.msftauth.net entered as exceptions in Exempted URLs. It says this option only applies to user traffic from known locations, and that if PAC files are used, exceptions must go in the PAC file exemption list or authentication fails; the PAC line it gives exempts only login.windows.net, login.microsoftonline.com and *.windowsazure.com.

quotes: 2. In the Authentication Exemptions section, enter the following exceptions in Exempted URLs, and click Add Items:

evidence.after: 2. In the Authentication Exemptions section, enter the following exceptions in Exempted URLs, and click Add Items:
quotes: - login.windows.net
- login.microsoftonline.com
- .windowsazure.com
- aadcdn.msauth.net
- aadcdn.msftauth.net
This option only applies to user traffic from known locations.
If you are using PAC files, enter the following exceptions in the PAC file exemption list. Otherwise, the authentication fails.
if (shExpMatch(host, "login.windows.net") || shExpMatch(host, "login.microsoftonline.com") || shExpMatch(host, "*.windowsazure.com")) return "DIRECT";

other-exempt-hosts.statement: The other guides name the hosts to enter in Exempted URLs in the Authentication Exemptions section: the required Okta domains (the Okta PAC example uses *.okta.com and *.oktacdn.com), the required PingOne domains, accounts.google.com for Google Workspace, app.onelogin.com for OneLogin, and the organization's AD FS URL for AD FS 3.0. The CA Single Sign-On guide instead says to enter the redirected URL in the PAC file exemption list, otherwise authentication fails.

quotes: In the Authentication Exemptions section, enter the required Okta domains in Exempted URLs.
If (shExpMatch(host, "*.okta.com", "*.oktacdn.com")) return "DIRECT";
In the Authentication Exemptions section, enter the required PingOne domains in Exempted URLs.
In the Authentication Exemptions section, enter accounts.google.com in Exempted URLs.
In the Authentication Exemptions section, enter app.onelogin.com in Exempted URLs.
In the Authentication Exemptions section, enter your organization's AD FS URL in Exempted URLs.
Enter the redirected URL to the PAC file exemption list. Otherwise, authentication fails.

pingone-scim-settings.statement: In PingOne the SCIM connection is created by selecting SCIM Outbound, with User Resource /Users, Group Resource /Groups, SCIM Version 2.0, Authentication Method OAuth 2 Bearer Token and Auth Type Header Bearer.

quotes: 5. Select SCIM Outbound and click Next.
User Resource: Enter /Users.
SCIM Version: Select 2.0.
Group Resource: Enter /Groups.
Authentication Method: Select OAuth 2 Bearer Token.
Auth Type Header: Select Bearer.

adfs-3-claims.statement: The AD FS 3.0 guide covers Windows Server 2012 R2 running Active Directory Federation Services 3.0 as the IdP. For the login-name claim it says to choose SAM-Account-Name if the Zscaler service hosts one domain for the organization and otherwise User-Principal-Name, and not E-Mail-Addresses, because users can have multiple email addresses and that could result in multiple user credentials; the outgoing claim types are Name ID and memberOf. It does not recommend Is-Member-Of-DL, because groups can be displayed as LDAP paths instead of group names, and says AD FS 3.0 federates all user groups by default.

quotes: This guide illustrates how to configure a Windows Server 2012 R2 running Active Directory Federation Services 3.0 (AD FS) as the identity provider (IdP) for the Zscaler service.
LDAP Attribute: Choose SAM-Account-Name if the Zscaler service is hosting one domain for your organization; otherwise, choose User-Principal-Name.
Zscaler doesn't recommend choosing E-Mail-Addresses because users can have multiple email addresses, and this could result in multiple user credentials in the Zscaler service.
Outgoing Claim Type: Choose Name ID.
Outgoing Claim Type: Enter memberOf.
Zscaler doesn't recommend choosing Is-Member-Of-DL because the groups can be displayed in the form of LDAP paths instead of the group name.
AD FS 3.0 federates all user groups by default.

adfs-2-claims.statement: The AD FS 2.0 guide covers Windows Server 2008 R2 running Active Directory Federation Services 2.0 as the IdP. It says to select SAM-Account-Name only if one domain is hosted by the Zscaler service, otherwise User-Principal-Name, and that AD FS 2.0 federates all the groups of a user by default.

quotes: This guide illustrates how to configure a Windows Server 2008 R2 running Active Directory Federation Services 2.0 (AD FS) as the identity provider (IdP) for the Zscaler service.
Select SAM-Account-Name only if you have one domain hosted by the Zscaler service. Otherwise, select User-Principal-Name.
AD FS 2.0 federates all the groups of a user by default.

casso-quirks.statement: The CA Single Sign-On guide covers CA SiteMinder version R12 SP3 CR5 as the IdP. It says the default CA SSO SAML portal URL might be unusable because RelayState is dropped, resolved by using the Redirect script; that Zscaler expects a POST Binding, which isn't the default for CA SSO; and that a CA SSO bug provides multi-valued Group data in an invalid format Zscaler can't use, handled with the FMATTR function.

quotes: This guide illustrates how to configure CA SiteMinder running version of R12 SP3 CR5 as the identity provider (IdP) for the Zscaler service.

You might not be able to use the default CA SSO SAML portal URL. A critical piece of information (RelayState) is dropped from the URL and the functionality fails. This is resolved by using the “Redirect script.”
Zscaler expects a POST Binding which isn't the default for CA SSO.
There is a bug in CA SSO where it provides the multiple values Group data in an invalid format/syntax that Zscaler can't use.
The key to handling Groups is to use the FMATTR function as shown below.

saml-only-guides-scim.title: Whether SCIM works with AD FS, OneLogin and CA SSO
saml-only-guides-scim.detail: The AD FS 3.0, AD FS 2.0, OneLogin and CA SSO guides describe SAML configuration only. That they say nothing about SCIM is an absence in those guides, not a statement that those IdPs cannot be used with SCIM.
